findings.title: A download fetched in place shows nothing while it runs, so the click looks dead until the whole file is saved
findings.failure: The fix round moved six links onto DownloadLink: the receipts' Report, the export review's PDF and CSV, the reviewer checklist's PDF and line CSV, the packet history's PDF and CSV, and the console export. A plain click now runs preventDefault and fetches the whole file with fetch() (download-link.tsx:178-185). The browser shows its download only after saveFile clicks a blob link, once the whole body has arrived. Meanwhile the link's only change is aria-busy (:208). No style reads aria-busy (git grep finds it only in loading-state.tsx). No text and no status message change either, and a second click is silently swallowed (:180-182). The plain <a> it replaced was a navigation, which showed the browser's own loading indicator from the click, and then its download as soon as the headers came. On Uploads the case is the slowest: while a batch's PUTs fill the connection, a receipt's Report fetch can take seconds with nothing on screen. The person may click again, conclude the link is broken, or leave. The product's own busy controls say what they are doing: ActionForm shows 'Working…' (action-form.tsx:112) and the screening form 'Sending…' (screening/upload-form.tsx:283). No shot shows this state (judged from code).
findings.fix:
Say the fetch in DownloadLinks' notice slot, where its refusal is said, so the sentences the links sit in (the reviewer checklist's) stay whole. DownloadLinks keeps a mounted, empty-when-idle `

` in that slot. While any DownloadLink inside it is fetching, the slot reads 'Downloading the file…'. The link reports busy through the same context it says refusals through. Keep aria-busy on the link and add `aria-busy:cursor-progress`. Clear the status on save or refusal; the refusal's alert then takes the slot as now. Files: components/download-link.tsx and download-link.test.tsx (a status case). No migration, no freeze exception, no founder or brand-owner decision.

findings.title: After a refused payer-and-contract pair, fixing the payer leaves the contract marked 'Error' until the letter is sent
findings.failure: In p.coverage.error-letter-contract.1280, .390 and .1280-dark at e36a68b, payer Q is shown with payer N's contract, and the contract is marked ('Error: Choose one of this payer’s contracts, or None named.', red border, aria-invalid, focused). If the person fixes the pair by changing the payer to N, LetterContractCheck sees a valid pair and clears its custom validity (letter-contract-check.tsx:24-27). But watchLetterMarks clears only the edited control's own mark (letter-marks.tsx:61-67), so the contract keeps its red 'Error:' line. A screen reader landing on it hears 'invalid entry' and that message for a contract that now belongs to the payer. The visible error also invites switching to None named, which would drop the contract the letter should name. The e2e codifies this ('the contract's mark stays until the letter is sent', download-refusals.spec.ts:191-193). This is the same rule UX-DLR-04 fixed for the edited control.
findings.fix: Clear a contract mark once the pair holds. In letter.tsx:204, give the contract's entry in LetterMarks the payer as a second trigger: { control: 'letter-contract', message: 'letter-contract-error', also: ['letter-payer'] }. In watchLetterMarks, a change of an `also` control clears that mark when `control.checkValidity()` is true (LetterContractCheck has just set its validity). Change the e2e step at spec:191-193 to expect the contract's mark gone after the payer change, and add a letter-marks unit case. Files: coverage/letter-marks.tsx, coverage/letter.tsx, coverage/letter.test.tsx, e2e/download-refusals.spec.ts. No migration.
